Replay

Explicit checkpoint conversion

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Authority and assetsAction-schema changesWorld-schema changesCombined world and action changes

checkpoint_decode and server_restore continue to require the current protocol, archive layout, schemas, model and application-supplied content ID. A failed load never guesses a conversion or changes the source bytes.

The first bridge is checkpoint_upgrade_v6(bytes, model, content, allocator). It accepts gameplay protocol 6 / checkpoint layout 4 and returns owned protocol-7 archive bytes, or an error and no output. Free a successful result with the same allocator. The input is borrowed, remains unchanged and can be released after conversion. This routine performs no I/O and opens no session.

Odin
converted, err := net.checkpoint_upgrade_v6(old_bytes, game.model(), game.CONTENT)
defer delete(converted)
if err != .None {return err}
// Decode and apply the application's identity, dependency and recovery policy
// before publishing or restoring the result.

Protocol 7 changes scheduled input packet framing. Its logical schemas, archive layout and model semantics remain compatible with protocol 6. The converter:

  1. Validates the original envelope, exact bounded section lengths, layout version, model values, roster, pending work and old protocol's complete contract hash.
  2. Computes the current contract from the same model and archived configuration.
  3. Changes the protocol/contract stamps and canonically re-encodes the archive.

The authority frame, tick, epoch, roster, held/future controls, queued actions, settled outcomes, bans and opaque admission-policy bytes are preserved. Scheduled and latest-observation models retain distinct contracts. Passing the wrong control timing fails. Passing an already-current archive also fails; this is a specific bridge rather than an idempotent generic loader.

The bridge only applies while the current protocol is 7. It does not convert older archive layouts, different state schemas, removed fields, changed gameplay content or application semantics. Those require explicit source-version types and a separately reviewed game conversion. Protocol-6 live peers still need a software update; a converted save does not let different protocol versions play together.

Authority and assets#

Conversion grants no authority and does not advance the epoch. Permit requirements and custom policy IDs remain present. server_restore still needs a newer epoch, a valid permit when required and the application's admission callback. Converting bytes changes their digest: an existing coordinator-approved checkpoint point or sealed handoff cannot simply be replaced by these bytes. Coordinated upgrade needs its own approved transition and publication under the new contract.

For a bundle, validate its old container, convert its root, then call assets.bundle_replace_root(original, converted, content). This preserves the asset records and payloads byte for byte and rebuilds the container's lengths and body digest. Check the root's content/epoch/tick against the container and verify all application dependencies before publication. A generic converter cannot infer which external assets a game's pending actions require.

The separate Scrapyard tool adds identity, complete current-frame spray dependencies, metadata and offline recovery checks. Its native regression gate uses genuine saves emitted by a retained protocol-6 game binary, with source hashes and exact resumed world hashes recorded in the conversion evidence.

Action-schema changes#

checkpoint_convert_actions(bytes, source_model, source_content, target_model, target_content, convert) handles an explicit application change to the action schema while retaining the same state/control types, seat count and control timing. It requires a current-protocol source archive. For a protocol-6 source, first use checkpoint_upgrade_v6 with the source model/content.

The converter validates the original archive and contract, maps each pending action, then computes the target contract and validates/encodes the result. Common world, roster, control, outcome, ban and policy sections are preserved. The mapper returns (new_action, ok); a false result or an invalid target accepted action fails the whole conversion without producing output. Missing required validation callbacks fail with Invalid_Model. Both models must provide an action handler when their archive contains accepted pending work.

Already refused requests can contain application-invalid values. A mapper should preserve their representable fields; the archive retains their original refusal reason and settlement frontier. They are not promoted into accepted requests. The target still enforces canonical schema validity for every encoded value.

The result is an owned byte buffer and the source is unchanged. This API does not convert world/control schemas, authorize a leader, advance epochs, reconstruct custom policy callbacks or infer which external assets the new content requires. Changing content also requires an explicitly updated bundle envelope; use bundle_replace_root(..., target_content=new_content) after checking application metadata and dependencies. Scrapyard's content-42 importer retains a frozen original action type and adds zeroed development payloads to the current action type. Event types may also differ: their schemas enter the target contract, but there is no serialized event history to transform. Scrapyard retains the content-42/43 event shape when importing into content 44.

World-schema changes#

checkpoint_convert_state(bytes, source_model, source_content, target_model, target_content, convert) maps a complete source world into a target world. The source must use the current protocol; controls, actions, events, seat count and control timing remain shared. Keep explicit source-version world types instead of making normal decode guess older layouts.

The mapper returns (target_world, ok). A refused mapping, invalid target world or insufficient restored egress budget fails without output. Full source validation precedes the mapper. Target contract/schema validation follows it. The frame tick, epoch, roster, held and future controls, pending actions, outcomes, bans and policy bytes remain intact. Output is owned; the borrowed source is unchanged. This conversion has the same authority and external-asset limitations described above.

Cavecrawl's explicit importer uses this boundary to add two captured floor definitions to an older Replay world. Its fixture is a real save produced by the earlier game binary, then converted and resumed by the current game in a fresh process.

Combined world and action changes#

checkpoint_convert(bytes, source_model, source_content, target_model, target_content, world_mapper, action_mapper) changes both world and action schemas in one explicit conversion. Controls, seat count and control timing stay shared; event types may differ because the archive contains no event history. Both mappers return (value, ok) and run only after complete source validation. A failed mapper or invalid target produces no output. The target must fit the restored egress budget.

The converter preserves frame tick, epoch, roster, held/future controls, pending action identities and refusal reasons, settled outcomes, bans and policy bytes. Rejected source actions can contain application-invalid fields; map their representable values without promoting them to accepted work. Source bytes are borrowed and unchanged; output is owned. The authority/asset limitations above still apply. Cavecrawl uses this path to add lobby state and commands while importing its two earlier Replay content versions. It does not attempt to import original Kit saves.
